row.evidence: ArcSight Platform docs integrate SSO with an external SAML 2.0 IdP but say a user present in the IdP must also exist in Core; authentication is built-in, SAML or LDAP, with no SCIM endpoint in the docs.
row.notes: New row. ArcSight is now sold by OpenText as the SIEM Platform (26.2), a customer-deployed platform (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud or off-cloud). opentext.com product pages return HTTP 444/490 to every fetch, and no public price list exists, so price fields are null and pricing_page_url points at the ArcSight documentation index. Authentication is built-in, SAML 2.0 (users must already exist in Core, so no JIT) or LDAP (users must exist in both systems); users can be imported from ArcSight ESM. The 26.2 docs table of contents (916 topics) and the 24.2 admin and user guides have no SCIM topic. REST APIs (OAuth2 client ID/secret) are documented per deployment; no public user-management endpoints were found. 'None' is by absence (rule 5).

plans.notes: Licensing is not published; opentext.com could not be loaded.

scim.notes: No SCIM topic in the SIEM Platform 26.2 table of contents or the ArcSight Platform 24.2 admin/user guides; users are created in the platform, imported from ESM, or authenticated through LDAP/SAML after they exist. 'false' is by absence (rule 5).

user_api.notes: ArcSight REST APIs (ArcMC, ACS, search, metadata, SOAR) use an OAuth2 client ID and secret, and their Swagger docs are served from each deployment, not publicly. No public user or group endpoints were found.

okta.notes: OIN search for 'arcsight' returned no integrations; ArcSight's SAML guide names Okta as an example external SAML 2.0 IdP.

fallbacks.other_sync: LDAP authentication (users must exist in both systems); import of users from ArcSight ESM

citations.quote: This section provides the steps to integrate SSO with an external SAML 2.0 IDP solution, such as NetIQ Advanced Authentication, Keycloak or Okta.

citations.title: Configuring SAML Authentication
citations.quote: A user present in the external SAML 2.0 IDP solution must also exist in Core to proceed with integration.

citations.title: Configuring LDAP Authentication
citations.quote: The identity provider (IDP) user and password has governance over the platform; therefore, the user must exist in both systems, but the password is validated only in LDAP.

citations.title: Password-Based Authentication
citations.quote: You can select built-in authentication or external authentication, such as SAML or LDAP.
